bugs: app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:30 checks whether the subscriber is already synced using the copy of the model loaded when the job was unserialized, before the WithoutOverlapping lock is acquired. So a job that was unserialized while another worker was finishing the same subscriber can get the lock afterwards, still see crm_synced_at as null, and POST the subscriber a second time. The window is small, but it is still a way to get the duplicates from symptom 2.

app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:22 loops over every unsynced subscriber, including ones already claimed and in flight, and runs one conditional UPDATE per row every minute. The query never filters out claimed rows, so while the queue is backed up the dispatcher does O(n) writes per run that do nothing.
antipatterns: tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:64-71 uses reflection on the #[Tries]/#[Backoff] attributes to check configuration values. That tests how the job is declared, not how it behaves, and breaks on harmless refactors.
app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:11 makes CLAIM_TTL_MINUTES public only so a test can read it.
tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:46-61 calls handle() and failed() by hand instead of running the job through a real worker, so nothing proves the job actually reaches failed_jobs.
strengths: Fixes all four root causes correctly: the catch-all that swallowed errors is removed and failed() is added; the dispatcher claims rows atomically with a stale TTL; withoutOverlapping(10) on the schedule; chunkById for the normalize command.

Uses current Laravel queue attributes (#[Tries], #[MaxExceptions], #[Backoff], #[DeleteWhenMissingModels]). I confirmed in vendor that they exist and are read. Combined with MaxExceptions, overlap releases don't eat into the exception budget.
WithoutOverlapping gets releaseAfter/expireAfter, so a crashed worker can't leave a per-subscriber lock stuck.
DeleteWhenMissingModels drops jobs for deleted subscribers without filling failed_jobs (confirmed with a probe test).
The change is small and stays close to the original code.

bugs: A job for a subscriber that has been deleted ends up in failed_jobs as a ModelNotFoundException (confirmed with a probe test). There is no deleteWhenMissingModels, which matters because failed_jobs is now the outage signal ops rely on. Minor.
antipatterns: tests/Feature/CrmSyncTest.php:113 asserts `where('email', 'like', '%[A-Z ]%')`. SQLite and MySQL LIKE don't support character classes, so this assertion can never fail.
app/Console/Commands/DispatchCrmSync.php:24 and :30 repeat the same stale-claim where-closure; one scope or local variable would remove the duplication.
app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:18 still uses the `$tries`/`$backoff` properties instead of the newer queue attributes. That's fine, but less current.

app/Jobs/SyncSubscriberToCrm.php:24 uses dontRelease(), which silently drops a job that overlaps another. This is acceptable because the TTL re-dispatch recovers it, but it is a less obvious choice than releaseAfter.
strengths: Fixes all four root causes: exceptions now propagate, with backoff and failed(); the dispatcher filters out claimed rows before claiming each one atomically; the schedule lock expires after 10 minutes; lazyById for the normalize command.
The job reads crm_synced_at with `fresh()` inside the overlap lock, which closes the stale-model duplicate race that impl-1 leaves open.
The dispatcher filters candidates in SQL before claiming them, so in-flight rows don't cause wasted writes on every run.

An end-to-end test runs real `queue:work` on the database queue and checks that the job lands in failed_jobs and that the subscriber syncs once the claim expires. That proves symptom 1 at the level ops actually see it.
Http::preventStrayRequests in beforeEach, and the in-flight test also checks re-queueing after the TTL with travel().

v.rationale: Both implementations find the same four root causes: the catch-all that swallowed exceptions (no retries, nothing in failed_jobs), the dispatcher re-queueing subscribers that were already queued, the default 24h withoutOverlapping lock on the schedule, and chunk() paging by offset over rows whose filter column it changes. Both fix them correctly, and both test suites pass (14 and 11 tests). Probe tests (an end-to-end outage then recovery on the database queue, a held overlap lock, a deleted subscriber, and 1100 rows through the dispatcher) passed on both. impl-1 uses more modern Laravel (queue attributes, MaxExceptions, DeleteWhenMissingModels). But its already-synced check reads a model loaded before the lock was acquired, which leaves a small window for duplicate POSTs, and its dispatcher runs a pointless UPDATE for every in-flight row every minute. Its tests also lean on reflection and calling handle() by hand. impl-2 reads the row with fresh() inside the lock, filters candidates in SQL, and proves symptom 1 with a real queue:work test that ends in failed_jobs. Its weaknesses are a vacuous LIKE assertion, a repeated where-closure, and deleted subscribers landing in failed_jobs. Overall impl-2 is ranked slightly higher, mainly for correctness against duplicates and for stronger tests.
